regs_in_letter: FD&C Act (no CFR section cited in letter text)

cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc subscale)
cases.claim: “Do you ever feel a bit “meh”?” | “~75% of people with depression may experience lingering effects of anhedonia, even on treatment” | “People taking Auvelity experienced a greater reduction in their anhedonia scores over 6 weeks vs placebo” | “More people taking AUVELITY achieved a 50% or greater improvement in their anhedonia scores over 6 weeks vs placebo”
cases.context: Image of smiling woman. Post hoc 5-item MADRS 'anhedonia rating sub-scale' (not validated, no type 1 error control). Disclaimer: “...the results could have occurred at random because the review of anhedonia data was not planned at the start of the study”.
cases.rationale: Implies a specific anhedonia benefit not demonstrated; post hoc unvalidated subscale; disclaimer does not cure.
cases.check: Rule: flag symptom-domain claims derived from post hoc subscales of the primary instrument; flag 'not planned'/'could have occurred at random' disclaimers as a signal of an unsupported claim.
